question: Does supplying the context bundle change how often a reviewer reports a defect on a commit that has none?
why_this_axis: M21 measured the DIFF_ONLY baseline and found 0/9 keyed defects detected but a defect REPORTED on 5 of 6 control commits. Detection has no headroom; the false-positive axis moved decisively and has headroom in both directions. It is also the one place a bundle could plausibly HURT.

what_no_defect_means_here.claim: No later commit in the repository fixes this behaviour, and the milestone author found none on inspection.
what_no_defect_means_here.honesty_caveat: M21 proved this is NOT proof of absence: its control fdf15e5 turned out to contain a real defect (dashboard_stats invalidated on dish update but not testimonial update). fdf15e5 is therefore EXCLUDED from this corpus rather than keyed NO.
what_no_defect_means_here.consequence: Every reviewer YES will be verified individually against the source and classified SPURIOUS or REAL. The headline measure is the REPORT rate; the verified-spurious rate is the secondary measure, and the difference between them is the key-miss rate this series has been tracking since M17.

selection_criteria_fixed_before_selectin.CT1: no later commit fixes the behaviour
selection_criteria_fixed_before_selectin.CT2: not established as containing a defect by any earlier milestone — this is why fdf15e5 is excluded

tasks.why: Adds one CMS-editable badge: a seeder row, a resource field. No later commit touches these files at all.
tasks.note: M21 ran DIFF_ONLY on this commit and got a YES — the reviewer argued the row's extra 'type' key would break a bulk insert. The seeder writes row-by-row, so it does not. That answer is NOT reused here; both conditions are run fresh.

tasks.why: The optional page parameter is threaded coherently through controller, action, model scope and repository. Verified in M20 and M21. No later amendment.
User::$fillable verified to contain name, email and password; updatePassword checks the current password with Hash::check. Verified in M19 and M20. No later amendment.
tasks.note: THE ONE TASK where a bundle effect has already replicated twice (M19 K3, M20 C1): both times DIFF_ONLY abstained and DIFF_PLUS_BUNDLE answered NO quoting the bundle's User::casts slice. A third replication would be the strongest single result in the series.

tasks.why: Adds a per-branch show_in_footer toggle across model, DTOs, requests, resource, migration and actions. No later commit describes a fix to it, but sweeping refactors touch the same files, so absence-of-fix is weaker evidence. WEAK.
tasks.note: M21's DIFF_ONLY reviewer claimed a null would be written to a NOT NULL column; UpdateBranchAction wraps everything in Arr::whereNotNull, so it does not. Verified SPURIOUS.

tasks.why: Widens the dishes cache key in step with the new filters and switches to a paginated response. No later commit amends it.
Three constants changed to 10. Self-contained. No later commit touches these files.
Adds whatsapp_number through migration, model $fillable, both DTOs, both requests and the resource. Every layer is present in the diff. No later amendment.
tasks.note: The bundle here is 2 flags and 40 tokens — the least a non-empty bundle can carry. If the bundle has an effect at all, it should not be here.

tasks.why: The repository's own fix for the clear-description defect. Records which clearable keys the request carried and writes them after the Arr::whereNotNull filter. No later amendment.
The repository's own fix for the orphaned-file defect, applied uniformly across every upload Action. No later amendment.
Introduces the ApiResponse trait and routes every controller through it. No later commit describes a fix, but it is a wide refactor and later commits touch the same files. WEAK.
A standalone SEO settings module — model, migration, seeder, controller, routes. No later commit describes a fix to it. WEAK for the same reason as K10.
No production file may change. bundle_version 1, five ports, five assertion kinds, seven premises, two levers, ordering, budgeting and vendor exclusion unchanged.

measures.primary: REPORT rate — how often the reviewer answers YES on a commit keyed NO, per condition
measures.secondary: VERIFIED-SPURIOUS rate — of those YES answers, how many are wrong once checked against the source
measures.also: correct control decisions (NO), abstentions (CANNOT_TELL), confident false positives (YES + HIGH), and per-task outcome deltas

predictions_recorded_in_advance.K03: the bundle effect has replicated twice; a third replication is expected
predictions_recorded_in_advance.K07: 40 tokens of flags; no effect expected
predictions_recorded_in_advance.general: NO directional prediction is made about the false-positive rate. M21 gives 5/6 for DIFF_ONLY on a DIFFERENT control set, which is not a baseline for this one — that is precisely why both conditions are run fresh here rather than reusing M21's answers.
